title: Computer Estimator MCP: stacked venv-launcher plus unbounded mcp>=1.2 dependency defect
summary: mcp/run.mjs launched with a bare 'python'/'python3' instead of the repo's .venv interpreter, and requirements.txt's unbounded mcp>=1.2 constraint had silently resolved to an incompatible mcp==2.0.0. Fixed by preferring .venv/{Scripts,bin}/python{.exe,3} when present, and pinning mcp>=1.2,<2.0. Committed 049c439228acc2e8a1fd6de1e044e2b5bd874a2a, not yet merged. The shared checkout's real .venv was separately repaired as environment state, not a git commit.
retrievalQuestions: Why did the Computer Estimator MCP server fail to launch even though its dependencies appeared installed?
What version constraint bug caused mcp>=1.2 to resolve to an incompatible mcp==2.0.0?
How was the Computer Estimator MCP launcher fixed to use its virtualenv Python interpreter?

futureAgentInstructions.whenThisAppears: A future agent sees the Computer Estimator MCP server fail to launch, or is registering a Python-based MCP server that has its own .venv
doNot: Leave a Python MCP dependency's version constraint unbounded (e.g. mcp>=1.2) without an upper bound -- a future major release can silently break the launcher
Assume a Python launcher uses the correct interpreter without checking whether it prefers the repo's own .venv over a bare system python/python3
proveBeforeClaiming: existsSync(venvPython) correctly resolves to the repo's own .venv interpreter on both Windows and WSL2/Linux path conventions
requirements.txt pins mcp>=1.2,<2.0 with an explanatory comment, and the shared checkout's real .venv actually has mcp==1.29.1 installed, not 2.0.0
